lines.en: Ben, after the storm had passed, I walked down to Granville Island to check the damage.
lines.pt: Ben, depois que a tempestade passou, desci até Granville Island para ver os estragos.

lines.en: Was it bad? As soon as the wind had dropped, I fell asleep, so I saw nothing.
lines.pt: Foi grave? Assim que o vento amainou, eu dormi, então não vi nada.

lines.en: Some trees had come down, and once the rain had stopped, the council started clearing the roads.
lines.pt: Algumas árvores tinham caído, e assim que a chuva parou, a prefeitura começou a limpar as ruas.

lines.en: Did the power come back quickly? Our street had no electricity until the crews had repaired the lines.
lines.pt: A energia voltou rápido? Nossa rua ficou sem eletricidade até as equipes consertarem a rede.

lines.en: Ours returned after the engineers had replaced a broken cable. Then I could finally charge my phone.
lines.pt: A nossa voltou depois que os engenheiros trocaram um cabo quebrado. Aí pude finalmente carregar o celular.

lines.en: I called my sister as soon as I had found a signal. She had been worried since the storm began.
lines.pt: Liguei para minha irmã assim que consegui sinal. Ela estava preocupada desde que a tempestade começou.

lines.en: Understandable. By the time I reached the harbour, the waves had calmed down and boats were moving again.
lines.pt: Compreensível. Quando cheguei ao porto, as ondas tinham se acalmado e os barcos voltavam a andar.

lines.en: Once the sun had come out, everything looked so peaceful. You would never guess what had happened.
lines.pt: Assim que o sol saiu, tudo parecia tão tranquilo. Ninguém imaginaria o que tinha acontecido.

lines.en: The owner of the coffee shop said he had boarded up his windows before the storm had even started.
lines.pt: O dono da cafeteria disse que tinha coberto as janelas com tábuas antes mesmo de a tempestade começar.

lines.en: Smart man. After we had cleaned up the garden, we found a neighbour’s fence in the middle of our lawn.
lines.pt: Homem esperto. Depois de limparmos o jardim, achamos a cerca de um vizinho no meio do nosso gramado.

lines.en: That sounds like a perfect excuse for a barbecue. Let’s invite everyone once the weather has settled.
lines.pt: Parece uma ótima desculpa para um churrasco. Vamos convidar todos quando o tempo tiver se firmado.

facts.big: after / once / as soon as + had + particípio
facts.label: Orações temporais
facts.sub: O fato que terminou antes vai para had + particípio: After the storm had passed, I went out. Conectores: after, once, as soon as, before, by the time.

facts.label: Depois que
facts.sub: Use after + had + particípio para o fato que terminou antes: After the storm had passed, I walked down. A segunda oração fica no passado simples. Em português, usamos só o pretérito.

facts.label: Assim que
facts.sub: As soon as dá a ideia de logo em seguida: As soon as the wind had dropped, I fell asleep. Troque as soon as por once se quiser um tom neutro. Ambos aceitam had + particípio.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: After the storm had passed shows the storm finished first.
We say “After the storm passed, I walked had”.
items.why: We say after the storm had passed, I walked.

items.s: Once and as soon as can also introduce the earlier action.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: After the storm had passed shows the storm finished first. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “After the storm passed, I walked had”. → Falso (We say after the storm had passed, I walked.)
Once and as soon as can also introduce the earlier action. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: The day after the storm · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Sunday morning in Vancouver, and the sky is pale blue. During the night, a strong storm crossed the coast. Elsa walks along the street with a coffee in her hand. Branches and leaves cover the pavement. She meets her neighbour Ben outside his house. They want to compare what each of them did.

“Ben, after the storm had passed, I walked down to Granville Island to check the damage.” says Elsa. “Was it bad? As soon as the wind had dropped, I fell asleep, so I saw nothing.” says Ben. “Some trees had come down, and once the rain had stopped, the council started clearing the roads.” says Elsa.
